name: Brand & Breakfast
business: Six rooms in an old stone house above a harbour, run by a host named Mara; breakfast included, a local guide, requests the host confirms by phone or email, payment at the house.
moment: Two moments in one: a guest before arrival (a room, dates, a request) and a guest already staying (breakfast hours, what's around here, a rainy day). Both want the host, not a website.
homePattern: A concierge desk: a time-of-day greeting with the host's name, the question "What can I do for you?", the things a guest wants as paper tiles with a round photo, then a pinned "Today at the house" notice and a guest perk (a coffee on us at the café down the hill).

elements.notes: The desk. The greeting is computed from the hour; the tiles' queries equal fixed screens' match queries; the today notice and the perk are static props the host edits, which is what makes the home relevant instead of decorative.

Exactly one room: a mounted photo, the name with the nightly rate stacked opposite, an italic description, a dotted-leader ledger (sleeps, bed, looks at, floor, size), then a reservation slip with date pickers, a guest count within the room's limit, an indicative total and one button that carries dates, nights and rate into the request.

One form for every request to the host: kind chips (book a room, early check-in, late check-out, a dinner table, pickup, something else); dates and guests only when it is a booking; name, phone, email, a note, the consent checkbox, "Send to Mara". The click query carries every field.
